Does a point lie on a Bezier curve?

Source: R/bezier.R
proportions_along_bezier_curve_for_point.Rd

proportions_along_bezier_curve_for_point() solves, for each coordinate, the Bezier polynomial minus the point's coordinate and returns the real roots in [0, 1] common to every coordinate: the parameters at which the curve passes through point. Roots are rounded to the number of decimals given by round_to before they are compared, as upstream does. point_lies_on_bezier() is TRUE when there is at least one such root.

Usage

proportions_along_bezier_curve_for_point(
  point,
  control_points,
  round_to = 1e-06
)

point_lies_on_bezier(point, control_points, round_to = 1e-06)

Arguments

point

A point, c(x, y, z).

control_points

Control points of the curve, an n x 3 matrix.

round_to

Rounding precision of the roots.

Value

A numeric vector of parameters (usually of length 0 or 1), or TRUE/FALSE.

Examples

cubic <- rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(1, 2, 0), c(3, -1, 0), c(4, 1, 0))
p <- bezier(cubic)(0.25)
proportions_along_bezier_curve_for_point(p, cubic)
#> [1] 0.25
point_lies_on_bezier(c(1, 1, 0), cubic)
#> [1] FALSE
